Name: 0_evaluators_did_reactions_looking
Representative_Docs: ['Since leaving the lab I have reflected some in my speech performance. I haven’t exactly been dwelling on what I could have done better but rather I have been focused on the sensory and emotional experience of going through such a simulation. The exercise made me think about real life scenarios and job prep. The high stakes situation of talking about an ideal job made the simulation more nerve wracking. It wasn’t just like doing any random interview for just any job. The evaluators being in a group was interesting and looking back it was clear I focused most on the guy on the left and kind of barely looked at the others.  I also randomly was intrigued by the experience bc this was the second time in my life using vr so I was also thinking about the novelty of that. I thought about the visual aspects of the evaluators specifically race, gender and age. I wondered how my experience would have been different had they been different in appearance. They were all white men with glasses which felt weird and random to me. After learning they’re European professors it made sense contextually but upon first encountering them I really wondered why the evaluators were represented as such.', 'Looking back at the speech task, I realized all the evaluators were white men. Based off of that alone, I immediately felt as thought I’d be taken less seriously. In the moment, negative facial reactions from them felt real and made me more nervous, but reflecting on the fact that they were AI evaluators does not leave me rethinking my performance much afterwards.', 'I wonder if every minute the 3 evaluators types of expressions changed. For example, the right evaluator looked very encouraging, nodding, smiling, while the left was yawning, looking annoyed/bored and almost angry or skeptical of what I was saying. And then about a minute later, it switched.  I almost couldn’t look away from the evaluators who looked negatively at me and I remember it tripped me up and distracted me from what I was trying to say. I remember pausing and stumbling over some words and kind of repeating myself because it was confusing. Because the face on the right became less comforting and then became neutral to negative. This made it feel very non-human because people don’t filter through emotions like that. Anyway, it felt very unsettling. I think yesterday I was trying to gain as much information about my evaluators by looking at them while I spoke, but it just left me feeling more confused by their array of emotions that seemed to change every minute. Yesterday after the study I felt very socially exhausted though I had to be in social environments. I also sort of felt exhausted emotionally today. I’ve gone over different parts of the lab in my mind and wondering how the n-back test or recognizing facial expressions related to the speech and also wondering how I did on the 2 n-back test before and after the speech. I think I did better the second time as my mind was maybe more engaged after the speech.']

Name: 1_public_improve_performance_ways
Representative_Docs: ["I haven't thought much about it. Looking back, the sudden changes in facial expressions was a bit funny and unrealistic. It made me think that I should improve my public speaking skills and it was a positive challenge for me.", 'I am currently undergoing EMDR therapy for a traumatic event unrelated to this study. My therapist and I ended up using a moment from the speech task -- where one of the interviewers looked away from me and yawned, causing me to trip over my words--as a "practice run" for reprocessing truly traumatic memories. I am proud of the way I was able to process my performance on the speech task immediately after the task, and found that reprocessing was helpful to dig into some of the ways the task felt threatening to my identity/self-worth. I have also used some of my daily meditation techniques to process feelings of disappointment, shame, and guilt related to slip-ups during the speech task.', "I felt pretty negatively about my speech performance after the task and I still feel negatively about it, but with time and continued thought about it comes acceptance that a weak performance doesn't requite negative thinking, and I'm finding ways to frame it in a positive light like 'now I know what things I can improve in the future'."]
